[spoiler=[b]The XF-36 Program Begins[/b]]

Near 9pm at night, a ship docks at a basic civilian port on Primank island, unloading a singular jet-black limousine from its ramp. The car wastes no time, driving off out of the port and into the night, a line of streetlights illuminating the lonely road as they pass intersections which seem to go to nowhere. Other lights appear as the car drives on, their sources hidden by vegetation only interrupted by the occasional sight of a barbed wire fence. In the back of the limo, two executives sit, wondering what the project they have been assigned to could have to do with this seemingly desolate island.

On the right sat Werner Andor representing NorthernStar. A college man with a degree in aerospace engineering and a knack for marketing, he was in good graces with Herman before his fall, and his connections got him well seated with the new governments military reforms. On the left was Gerchen Fred, a pilot turned unscrupulous businessman with quite a number of controversies to his name while working for Lockgates. Both of these men sat in the back of the long car, pouring from a bottle of Lavian wine, so-called Île des Vignes Royales as they passed more and more obscured lights and lonely intersections. 

The silence of the car ride was interrupted once the men couldn't stand it anymore, Gerchen opened his mouth first. We are here for a plane! Youd think they were going to kill us with how abandoned this place is. Werner prepared a response as he finished his glass, observing Gerchen staring out into the night, almost in contempt, as if it was the Lavian Governments plan to personally offend him. Relax Gerchen. We are here for quite the project, dont you think governments value their privacy with things like this? The only response from Werners fellow representative was an annoyed side eye and a hrmph. 

After another short stint of yet more silence, Werner decided to stimulate his mind with something other than the provided wine. Driver, could you perhaps turn on the radio? Its getting quite dull back here. The driver simply nodded and reached for the volume knob, pressing in on it to turn the radio on. Immediately the words of a song came through the speakers, its melodic words floating through the car as they drove on. Keep smiling through, just like you always do, till the blue skies drive the dark clouds far away. So will you please say hello, to the folks that I know? Tell them I wont be long. Theyll be happy to know, that as you saw me go, I was-Id take the silence over this! Gerchen blurted out, somewhat annoyed at the song selection of the station they were listening to. Is there anything else they broadcast on this island? The driver looked up at the rear view mirror for a second before responding. Im sorry sir, all the other stations are quiet at this time of night, unless the local airports weather report is a choice.

The ride continued in silence until lights in the distance got larger and larger. A complex of hangers, warehouses, and various facilities emerged from the darkness, protected simply by a guard post on the road with some razor wire fencing. Stopping at the post, the driver handed an ID over to a tired man in Lavian Airforce uniform and made some quiet smalltalk, gesturing to the two representatives in the back. After glancing slightly into the vehicle, the guard handed the ID back and raised the gate, allowing them access. They drove past various buildings and empty parking areas until arriving at a hangar with a few cars parked outside of it. Parking near the side entrance, the two men stepped out of the car and were quickly greeted by a youngish looking man wearing a dress uniform. Welcome to Primank Military Island! I hope the drive was satisfactory. The representatives nodded before following the fellow into the hangar. Blinded by the sudden light, their eyes slowly adjusted to see the massive workspace, crowded with assembly equipment and prototype aircraft in various levels of completion. This is a little view of the rapid prototyping lab we will be producing the concepts for the XF-36 once everyone can come together and decide what options well have built to test. The man doesnt even wait for a response before turning back to face the representatives. We have quarters arranged for you in a local coastal town not too far from here. Great views if I do say so myself.

With that, the representatives get back into their car and begin their journey to their temporary houses. What an odd man, Gerchen would remark as he climbed back into the waiting limo. Werner would nod. He is probably being pressured by his higher ups. Its common to see someone rush things when that happens. Well get more time to look at that assembly area when we finally meet the other representatives anyway.Always on the positive, huh Werner? [/spoiler]

[i][b]ARLAN VOS AS PREMIER AGAIN - The Express - Naerim, Tirakan[/b][/i]

The results of Tirakan's presidential re-election were formally confirmed last night, concluding the countrys first full electoral cycle since reunification and marking a decisive victory for incumbent Premier Arlan Vos.

In the first round of voting, Vos secured 50% of the vote, narrowly missing an outright majority. His challengers followed at a distance, with Lilien Ilryie receiving 23%, Baki Deniz 18%, and Adil Öztirak 9%. As no candidate crossed the 50-percent threshold, a run-off election was triggered between Vos and Ilryie. The run-off delivered a clear mandate. Arlan Vos won with 73% of the vote, while Lilien Ilryie finished with 27%. In his victory address held in the Heron Plazza, in Naerim, Vos framed the result as confirmation of a national course. He stated that the electorate had chosen to "finish what was started," referring to the reconstruction and strategic repositioning of Tirakan following three decades of civil war.
Vos pledged to complete the reintegration of the Ashkaf Isles, describing their return as both a strategic and historical priority. He also confirmed plans to further expand Tirakan's gas exports, positioning the country as a long-term energy anchor for not only the Shamats, but for the world.
On the economic front, Vos emphasized the next phase of industrial policy. He promised continued investment in semiconductors, advanced computing, artificial intelligence, drone manufacturing, and other high-value industries, with the stated goal of "making Tirakan great again". At the same time, he stressed that traditional pillars, gas, logistics, defense manufacturing, steel, and rare earth processing, would remain central and more relevant then ever before, to the economy.
In foreign policy, Vos reaffirmed his intention to take a more assertive anti-colonial stance across Shamat, while improving diplomatic relations with a broad range of partners. He singled out Tirakan's neighbors, Valddera and Shahban, as priorities for stabilization and described Vespurias as one of Tirakan's closest and most trusted partners.
He also announced that preparations were underway for the second major trade corridor, aimed at linking Tirakan with markets in Elseyr, building on the momentum of the first corridor initiative. According to Vos, the objective is to make Tirakan "economically unavoidable" through connectivity.
Addressing energy policy, Vos confirmed that the civilian nuclear energy program remains on track, with completion expected earlier than the promised 2030. He reiterated the government's position that the program is civilian in nature, focused on benefiting the common good.
Finally, Vos introduced what he described as his next pet initiative: A push to re-establish open trade agreements with every willing country worldwide, reversing decades of isolation and positioning Tirakan as a global trade turntable.

The scale of the run-off victory is being interpreted domestically as a strong signal of political consolidation. With a renewed mandate and limited opposition leverage, Arlan Vos now enters his new term with significant authority to shape Tirakan once more.
